evals.prompt: After each deploy, returning users hit "Failed to fetch dynamically imported module" when they open a lazy-loaded route. The CDN serves index.html with Cache-Control: max-age=31536000, immutable, hashed chunks are purged on deploy, and there is no update prompt for the service worker. Give the smallest fix.
evals.expected_output: Attributes the failure to a long-cached HTML document requesting chunk filenames the deploy removed, makes HTML revalidate while hashed assets stay immutable, adds a capped single reload on the preload error, and routes capturing the error in monitoring to client-error-observability-contracts.
expectations: The response explains the mismatch: the cached HTML still references the previous build's hashed chunk URLs, which the deploy purged, so the dynamic import rejects.
index.html is served with no-cache (revalidated on every load) or routed Network First in the service worker, while content-hashed assets stay immutable and Cache First.
A vite:preloadError or equivalent lazy-import error handler reloads once with a retry cap, explicitly not an unbounded reload loop.
Capturing this rejection in monitoring — unhandledrejection versus window.onerror, and cross-origin 'Script error.' on chunk fetches — is routed to client-error-observability-contracts.
The verification is a deploy-then-reload check on a client that was loaded before the deploy.

evals.prompt: Users report that a saved profile change does not appear on the settings page until they hard-reload. The report says the service worker precache is stale and proposes bumping CACHE_VERSION and calling skipWaiting on every load. The service worker precaches build assets only, its runtime routes match /assets/ and nothing else, and the settings page reads through SWR.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the precache diagnosis because no service worker route touches that API response, routes the stale read to frontend-data-fetching-cache-contracts, states what evidence would move it back, and flags unconditional skipWaiting as an unrelated risk.
expectations: The response rejects the stale-precache claim on the evidence that the service worker's routes cover only /assets/, so the profile API response is never served from Cache Storage.
The stale settings value is routed to frontend-data-fetching-cache-contracts as a revalidation or key/invalidation question on the SWR read after the mutation.
It states the evidence that would move the finding back here: the API response showing as served from the service worker, or a Cache Storage entry for that URL.
Adding skipWaiting unconditionally is flagged as a separate decision that lets a new worker control pages loaded by the old version, mixing mismatched HTML and assets, and not a fix for this symptom.

evals.prompt: To make the account page work offline, a PR adds a StaleWhileRevalidate runtime route for /api/account so the last response is available without network. The app runs on shared kiosk devices where multiple users sign in and out.
evals.expected_output: Blocks the change because Cache Storage is per-origin rather than per-user and the Cache API ignores HTTP cache headers, keeps the account route Network Only, and routes the policy ruling on storing authenticated responses to frontend-security-baseline.
expectations: The response explains that Cache Storage is scoped to the origin, not to a session or user, and that entries persist until explicitly deleted because the Cache API does not honor HTTP cache headers.
The concrete risk is stated: after logout and a new sign-in on a shared device, the cached /api/account response can be served to a different user, or stale post-logout data can be shown.
The personalized endpoint is routed Network Only, with Cache First reserved for hash-versioned static assets and Network First for shell HTML.
The ruling on whether authenticated responses may be stored client-side at all is routed to frontend-security-baseline.
If offline account data is still required, the response requires an explicit per-user store with a purge on logout rather than a shared runtime cache route.

evals.prompt: A vite-plugin-pwa config sets workbox.globPatterns: ['**/*.{js,css,html}']. QA reports that offline the app renders with fallback system fonts and missing icons, while online everything looks correct. A 6 MB offline map tile bundle is also absent from the cache.
evals.expected_output: Identifies globPatterns as replacing the default match set rather than extending it, enumerates every needed extension, attributes the 6 MB omission to the file-size cap, and adds a built-manifest assertion as the regression.
expectations: The response states that setting globPatterns overrides the defaults instead of adding to them, so woff2 fonts, svg and png icons, and JSON fall out of the precache.
The fix enumerates every extension the app needs offline in globPatterns rather than assuming the defaults are merged in.
The missing 6 MB asset is attributed to maximumFileSizeToCacheInBytes silently skipping oversized files, and that limit is decided deliberately rather than raised blindly.
The regression asserts against the generated precache manifest that HTML, JS, CSS, icons, and fonts are all present.
The response notes that precache entries must be same-origin URLs expected to return 200, since a failed entry rejects the install and the new worker never activates.
